text:
anya: Heads-up — ACME asks for unlimited burst credits + per-route priority for Dedicated.
jamie: yikes. unlimited is a hard no from infra side. what are they defending vs expected traffic spikes?
morgan: sales says they want a single SLA for the whole account. they've seen big variance across routes and want a safety valve for peaks.
anya: proposal idea: priority-lane add-on with a softcap model. allows bursts up to X% of baseline for N hours, then fall back.
liz: finance prefers committed tiers + purchasable burst packs. softcap OK if we can meter and bill predictably. need sample numbers.
jamie: from runtime: priority-lane = separate queue + preemptible slots. implementation effort ~2 sprints if we reuse existing qos sharding.
pricing-bot: Suggested config (rough):
```
base_tier: Standard
baseline_qps: 10k
priority_addon: priority-lane
burst_allowance: 3x baseline for 2 hours
fallback: degrade to v-small model or queue
price: $0.02/token prioritized
```
anya: rough launch criteria I want captured: 1) k6 traffic sim shows <150ms p95 under 3x bursts for 1hr, 2) billing event produced per-burst, 3) console UI for per-route enable + clear costs.
morgan: customer wants unlimited bursts during onboarding period for 3 months. can we offer a trial credit bridge instead?
liz: trial credits + conditional overage waiver for first 90 days is doable, but must be limited to $X per account and flagged in contract.
jamie: engineering risk: fallback fidelity. if we fallback to smaller model we need prompt-preserving transforms to avoid quality drops. that's another story.
anya: action items: @jamie estimate effort for QoS queue + fallback hooks, @liz define dollar cap and contract language, @morgan negotiate trial-credit ceilings with ACME, I'll write a spec for the UI and rollout gating.
pricing-bot: Note: record created -> PRD link: https://redwood/internal/prd/sku-entitlement-1711000000 (draft)
morgan: ack, I'll push customer expectations down to $50k cap for trial credit.
liz: fine if we gate it behind legal sign-off + commit to audit logs.
anya: quick question — do we want the priority add-on to be per-route or account-wide? per-route gives granularity but increases billing complexity.
jamie: per-route is doable but increases routing table size. I'd start account-wide then iterate to per-route in 2.
morgan: customer specifically asked per-route for one endpoint only. could do account-wide for GA and enable per-route during pilot.
anya: agreed. I'll add that to the PRD and flag rollout policy: pilot=per-route opt-in, GA=account-wide paid add-on.
liz: also add contract clause: "burst credits are advisory; overages beyond negotiated cap billed monthly" + auditability.
anya: thanks — will circulate PRD tomorrow. short follow-up sync at 11?
morgan: joining.
jamie: joining.
pricing-bot: Thread closed by bot: checklist created in /tasks/1711000000-checklist
